panels.description: Current burn height spread across actor-self-reported node metrics. A value above zero is disagreement, not automatically a defect.
panels.title: Burn-height spread

panels.description: Current Stacks tip spread across nodes. This remains meaningful even if an adversarial actor lies: drill down to see the outlier and compare orchestrator evidence.
panels.title: Stacks-height spread

panels.description: Scrape reachability of node, signer, and orchestrator-observed event endpoints.
panels.title: Metric endpoints reachable

panels.description: Number of currently active actor-targeted fault series reported by the authenticated event bridge.
panels.title: Active fault targets

panels.description: Latest failed orchestrator-observed invariants. Zero is healthy; failures remain visible until the invariant is observed passing again.
panels.title: Failed invariants

panels.description: Most recent measured recovery duration for the selected network.
panels.title: Last recovery duration

panels.description: Self-reported Bitcoin burnchain height by actor. Kept on its own scale because Stacks 3.x blocks advance much faster than burn blocks.
panels.title: Burn-chain cohort progress

panels.description: Self-reported canonical Stacks tip height by actor, independently scaled from the slower Bitcoin burnchain.
panels.title: Stacks-chain cohort progress

panels.description: Authenticated orchestrator fault, verification, and Kubernetes-admitted readiness state. Actor metrics cannot write these series.
panels.title: Fault, invariant, and runtime timeline

panels.description: Legacy P2P neighbor gauges from each node. This panel intentionally uses current-main transport metrics and has no libp2p dependency.
panels.title: Legacy P2P connectivity

panels.description: Signer proposal intake and response outcomes. Policy rejection and validation rejection detail depends on metrics available in the selected image.
panels.title: Signer proposal and vote rates

panels.description: Real per-signer response latency dispersion. Empty series mean the selected release does not expose the histogram or no proposals have completed.
panels.title: Signer response latency p95

panels.description: Actor-self-reported error and warning rates. A malicious binary can falsify these; use them as evidence, not authority.
panels.title: Node warning/error signals (self-reported)

panels.description: Latest orchestrator-observed invariant state. Use the durable HTML timeline for the complete event payload and replay instruction ID.
panels.title: Invariant status

panels.description: Raw stdout/stderr from actor containers. Kubernetes identity labels are collector-attached; every log body is untrusted, adversarial actor-self-reported content and must not be treated as authoritative.
panels.title: Actor logs (untrusted content; Kubernetes-attached identity)

panels.description: Kubernetes-observed actor census. Role, node placement, Pod phase, and admitted image are trusted orchestration metadata. Select an actor variable and follow the Actor drill-down link for detail.
panels.title: Trusted actor inventory and placement

panels.description: Latest trusted Kubernetes readiness and restart count for the selected cohort. Restarts are shown numerically; readiness uses green/red state.
panels.title: Trusted runtime health by actor

panels.description: Current self-reported chain tips by node actor. Sort by either height to identify a lagging cohort; corroborate suspicious actors with trusted readiness and logs.
panels.title: Node chain cohort (actor self-reported)

panels.description: Runloop initialization and current/next reward-cycle registration for every signer. This is an availability map, not a weighted quorum calculation.
panels.title: Signer participation matrix (self-reported)

panels.description: Aggregate block-production, receipt, processing, and serving rates. Separation between these curves locates the stage at which network progress stopped.
panels.title: Network block pipeline (actor self-reported)

panels.description: Peer counts by actor. Use this distribution to distinguish an isolated node from a network-wide partition. Current-main legacy transport only.
panels.title: P2P connectivity distribution (self-reported)

panels.description: Orchestrator-observed FaultCampaign phases. A new labelled series is created only when the controller-observed phase changes; Chaos Mesh bookkeeping alone cannot produce Passed.
panels.title: Fault campaign state (trusted)

panels.description: Current sealed AttacknetRun identity, phase, attribution state, and replay status. The schedule digest ties this view to the immutable execution artifact.
panels.title: Attacknet run state and schedule (trusted)

panels.description: Trusted effect and recovery outcomes for exact admitted actors. Failed or Inconclusive rows are triage entry points; actor logs cannot create these results.
panels.title: Fault effect and recovery assertions (trusted)

panels.description: Current raw budget use by run. Values have the unit named by each series (counts, seconds, or percent); compare against the admitted AttacknetRun limits in its CR.
panels.title: Run budget use (trusted)

panels.description: Terminal counterfactual classifications from the run controller. FailureAbsent requires explicit evaluation; missing or ambiguous assertion evidence is Inconclusive. These are empirical fresh-network results and never causal-minimality claims.
panels.title: Fresh-network minimization outcomes (trusted)

panels.description: Per-signer weight visible to the current global-state evaluator. A healthy baseline has maximum exact-view support at or above the rounded-up canonical threshold on every signer. The separate evaluator threshold exposes the current floor/ceiling protocol inconsistency instead of hiding it.
panels.title: Signer global-state support (self-reported)

panels.description: Legacy coordinator round outcomes and unique signer weight accepted, effectively rejected, or independently classified as unavailable. Unavailable weight overlaps rejected_effective on current main; it is not discounted or renormalized.
panels.title: Legacy coordinator rounds and response weight

panels.description: Monotonic publish-to-answer latency to the first valid signer response, plus proposal-round latency to a weighted decision threshold. Both include StackerDB upload latency. Comparing their distributions helps diagnose weighted-tail/quorum accumulation delay, but subtracting aggregate quantiles is not a per-proposal delta. Timeout and chain-change exits intentionally do not claim thresholds.
panels.title: Proposal response and threshold latency

panels.description: Bounded Nakamoto block ingress, P2P relay handoff, and completed HTTP serving rates. A block may cross multiple boundaries; do not sum all series as unique blocks. All values are actor-self-reported.
panels.title: Nakamoto block transfer boundaries

panels.description: Render-time instrumentation declarations plus the immutable static or rolling version profile observed by the controllers. unavailable means missing Workstream M series are an expected capability gap, represented by an empty result rather than a healthy zero. A declared A11 profile supersedes the original scrape-profile expectation for absence alerts. Verify these declarations against the sealed capability manifest, admitted Pod UID, revision, config, provenance, and runtime image evidence.
panels.title: Instrumentation capability and version declarations

panels.description: Identity-bound baseline, active-fault, and recovery assertion outcomes emitted by the run controller. Violated means a trusted protocol value crossed its bound; Inconclusive means required actor evidence remained unavailable through its deadline. Actor log content cannot create either result.
panels.title: Protocol assertion gates (trusted)

panels.description: Exact admitted Pod, runtime image, Service, and evidence class used by each trusted protocol assertion. Use these rows to correlate a failed gate with actor logs and runtime state without trusting actor-supplied identity labels.
panels.title: Protocol assertion source identities (trusted)

panels.description: Orchestrator-observed lifecycle for each typed stage action. Burnchain reorg actions become Active only after the worker proves the replacement branch canonical; Pod existence alone is insufficient.
panels.title: Typed fault action lifecycle (trusted)

panels.description: Canonical height reported by each admitted Bitcoin policy clock. Height is separate from branch identity and cumulative work because those signals have different scales.
panels.title: Bitcoin heights

panels.description: Connected peer and locally-known branch-tip counts for each admitted Bitcoin node. Use with the branch-cohort panel to distinguish transport isolation from an actual competing branch.
panels.title: Bitcoin graph health

panels.description: A bounded 52-bit visualization fingerprint of each full best-block hash. Equal values indicate the same branch; full hashes remain in protocol evidence and are never metric labels.
panels.title: Bitcoin branch fingerprints

panels.description: Base-2 logarithm of cumulative work. It is suitable for cohort visualization only; exact 256-bit chainwork remains in structured assertion evidence.
panels.title: Bitcoin cumulative work (log2)

panels.description: Bounded 52-bit visualization fingerprints from identity-bound, actor-self-reported Stacks /v2/info observations used by each run gate. Equal values indicate the same burn view; full consensus hashes and exact heights remain in structured protocol evidence.
panels.title: Bound Stacks burn-view fingerprints

panels.description: Trusted topology-operator view of Bitcoin nodes, directed persistent P2P edges, and Stacks actor bindings. Compare this intended graph with actor-reported peer counts and branch state during partitions.
panels.title: Admitted Bitcoin graph and Stacks bindings (trusted)

panels.description: Topology-owned rolling upgrade state. Each labelled transition is joined to the immutable version and runtime-image tables above; Failed and Inconclusive campaigns roll back before reaching a terminal phase.
panels.title: Rolling upgrade lifecycle (trusted)

panels.description: Topology-operator-observed testing policy, immutable policy digest, requested egress profile, and isolated observer readiness. This is admitted orchestration state, not a claim that the signer executed the behavior.
panels.title: Admitted adversarial signer policies (trusted)

panels.description: Testing-only signer counters transported through the normal metrics endpoint. Values are actor-self-reported and show bounded evaluations and matches only; they do not establish impact or recovery. Use trusted campaign assertions and protocol gates.
panels.title: Deterministic policy state (self-reported)
